title: The month potato prices fell across India
summary: In February 2010, the median potato market moved -24.9% in a month, 7.0 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 7.0σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for potato, across 397 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: February 2010
scenes.caption: Potato prices across 397 markets that reported in both January 2010 and February 2010.

scenes.headline: Median move -24.9%
scenes.caption: The typical market's potato price fell 24.9% in one month. 97% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 7.0× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 7.0 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Jharkhand
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 21 reporting markets in Jharkhand had a median change of -35.7%.

scenes.headline: Gurgaon
scenes.caption: Gurgaon (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹550 → ₹350 per quintal (-36.4%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
